research.title: Brookfield’s Connor Teskey on the Real Bottleneck in the AI Buildout
research.summary: The bottleneck in the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout is neither capital nor demand, but rather the operational capability to develop land, secure a grid connection, and build the power supply, says Brookfield Asset Management CEO Connor Teskey on Goldman Sachs Exchanges: Great Investors. Indeed, one market misconception is that demand for data centers is somehow “fragile,” he says in this conversation with Alison Mass, chairman of Investment Banking in Goldman Sachs Global Banking & Markets. Teskey also shares his perspective on long-term investing, Brookfield's approach to building businesses, and the evolution of its private credit platform.

research.title: Bullish Options Trades Slow amid AI Uncertainty
research.summary: Options markets are showing signs of increased nervousness about artificial intelligence (AI) as investors focus closely on earnings from large tech companies and try to separate likely winners from losers, says Lee Coppersmith from the Equity Derivative Sales team in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Overall demand for AI stocks remains strong and the S&P has remained resilient, but put option buying has picked up in recent weeks while activity has waned in call options that would reward a jump in equities, he explains on The Markets podcast.
